{
  "key": "pr-1775",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged."
  }

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
          # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.

echo "Build info generated:"

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
          # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` counts attempts from the `for` header, so a budget change would still be caught — this only removes the second place the number lives.

{
  "key": "pr-1775",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged."
  }

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1775._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` line 477

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `[ "$attempt" = "4" ]` hardcodes the loop length — keep it derived, not duplicated**

gh-1149 was itself a hardcode-desync bug (`--retry 3` treated as "3 total"). This line must now stay manually in sync with `for attempt in 1 2 3 4` above; if the list is ever bumped without updating the literal, the last attempt loses its sleep and the final failure message fires early (cosmetic today, but it is exactly the class of drift this step's history punishes).

Suggested: derive the last attempt from the list itself:

```bash
attempts=(1 2 3 4)
for attempt in "${attempts[@]}"; do
  ...
  if [ "$attempt" = "${attempts[-1]}" ]; then
    echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
  ...
```

`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` counts attempts from the `for` header, so a budget change would still be caught — this only removes the second place the number lives.

---

### Thread 2 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` line 484

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: redirect-error noise when `$ZIP` does not exist**

If all 4 attempts die before curl creates the file (e.g., connect failures), `wc -c < "$ZIP"` fails on the stdin redirect, which bash processes **before** `2>/dev/null` applies — so a stray `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-<arch>.zip: No such file or directory` leaks into the log even though the `|| echo 0` fallback handles it correctly (behavior is right: `got=0` → keep branch → exit 1).

If you want clean logs, prefer a form where the guard is part of the command:

```bash
got=$( [ -f "$ZIP" ] && wc -c < "$ZIP" | tr -d ' ' || echo 0 )
# or on macOS: got=$( stat -f%z "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null || echo 0 )
```

Behavior-affecting alternative: none needed — the current code is correct; this is log hygiene only.

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` line 441

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: concurrent same-arch runs can still interleave `-C -` writers into this persisted zip**

`concurrency.group` is per-ref (`Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`), and this machine hosts multiple agent slots — so a daily-publish leg and a manual/tag build from different refs can overlap on this runner. Two same-arch jobs would then run two `curl -C -` writers into this same per-arch path; the digest gate converts the worst case into a purge + exit 1 (both runs red that day, next run self-heals from a clean partial), so it is bounded — but worth a sentence in the comment, or a cheap `flock`/lockdir around the loop if the overlap ever materializes:

```bash
exec 9>"$ZIP.lock"
flock -w 600 9 || exit 1
```

Not worse than the pre-PR state (the old pre-loop `rm -f` also unlinked the other writer's in-flight file); the per-arch rename incidentally removed the cross-workflow collision with build-mobile's arch-less `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`, leaving this the only remaining (self-healing) overlap.

{
  "key": "pr-1775",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged."
  }
}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

gh-1149 was itself a hardcode-desync bug (`--retry 3` treated as "3 total"). `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` counts attempts from the `for` header, so a budget change would still be caught — this only removes the second place the number lives.

💡 **SUGGESTION: redirect-error noise when `$ZIP` does not exist**

{
  "key": "pr-1775",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged."
  }
}

durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the

  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1775
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1775
- **Title**: gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1759` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -80
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:57:54Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T01:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged.

gh-1149 was itself a hardcode-desync bug (`--retry 3` treated as "3 total"). This line must now stay manually in sync with `for attempt in 1 2 3 4` above; if the list is ever bumped without updating the literal, the last attempt loses its sleep and the final failure message fires early (cosmetic today, but it is exactly the class of drift this step's history punishes).

Suggested: derive the last attempt from the list itself:

```bash

  ...
  if [ "$attempt" = "${attempts[-1]}" ]; then
    echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2

`test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` counts attempts from the `for` header, so a budget change would still be caught — this only removes the second place the number lives.

💡 **SUGGESTION: redirect-error noise when `$ZIP` does not exist**

{
  "key": "pr-1775",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1759 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #1759
### Root Cause
The `cli` leg failed in build-macos.yml's "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step: the 97,238,501-byte upstream asset arrived at 40–108KB/s while the retry budget (3 × 240s attempts) was sized for gh-1149's good-day ~300KB/s — only 29.5% (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) was received, then `exit 1`. Resume itself worked (`Resuming transfer from byte position …` in the logs), but the pre-loop `rm -f "$ZIP"` discarded each run's partial, so no daily run ever banked durable progress. The cache fallback was cold too: the `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` entry saved 10-20 06:02Z was LRU-evicted by the repo's daily cache churn before 10-21 19:03Z (both jobs logged `Cache not found`).

### Previous Attempt
gh-1149 (already in-tree) fixed the earlier `curl --retry` off-by-one against the 15-min step cap and added `-C -` resume. Its invariants are kept — but its budget assumed ~300KB/s and treated the partial zip as single-run state, which this run disproves.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step): the per-arch `/tmp` partial zip now **persists across runs** — `-C -` resumes it within the step and across daily runs; a pre-loop sha256 gate skips the download entirely when the persisted zip is already complete (also avoids the HTTP-416 trap of resuming a whole file); an incomplete download **keeps** the partial (size < pinned 97,238,501) so the next run resumes from its byte offset; only wrong-content (size/sha mismatch on full bytes) is **purged**, so a corrupt partial cannot wedge the step. Budget raised to 4 × 240s attempts under a 20-min step cap (worst case 975s + 60s reserve = 1035s ≤ 1200s).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart`: pins the new invariants (persistence, keep-vs-purge by pinned byte size + sha256, pre-loop gate); RED against the pre-fix workflow (2 of 5 fail), GREEN after.

### Test Coverage
- `dart test test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5 passed (fails 2/5 against the old workflow).
- Behavioral sim of the extracted step script against a throttled (80KB/s) Range-capable server: old script's partial never grew past 3 attempts across runs (the treadmill); new script run 1 exited 1 keeping a 983,040-byte partial, run 2 resumed from byte 983,040 → digest OK → unzipped, run 3 with the server dead skipped the download via the persisted-zip gate, and corrupt-complete/oversize partials were purged.

### Notes
- First green run re-warms `actions/cache`; until then the persisted partial carries progress across daily runs, so slow-link days converge instead of restarting from byte 0.
- ci.yml / nightly.yml WasmRun steps run on GitHub-hosted runners (600s attempts, datacenter links) — intentionally unchanged."
  }
}

            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
